findings.reason: §4's retirement claim and §7's "keyed by machine" resolver plan are both under-scoped until they name `_supply_probe_orientations` and the `mast.json` path and fold them into the same catalogue-driven source, or the branch is retired in one file and re-joined in another.
findings.text: §4 asserts that resolving store format, root and probe-angle source from the catalogue will retire `description_reader.py:103`'s `machine == "mast"` branch "not joined by a second", but a second MAST-only probe-angle source lives at `_supply_probe_orientations` (line 266), which the §7 stamp route passes through: `TransformGeometrySource.table_for` calls `read_geometry_table(shot_id, store_root=self.store_root)` (line 325) with `machine`/`store_format` defaulting to MAST's zarr, and `TransformGeometrySource.revision` hard-codes `PACKAGED_MACHINE_MAP_ROOT / "mast.json"` (line 362). §7 keys only the shot set by machine; the class itself carries three further MAST hard-codings — the reader defaults, `revision`'s catalogue path, and `provenance`'s `"store_format": "zarr"` — that the JT-60SA stamp must displace.

findings.reason: the fork is deliberate, justified by dependency direction, limited to one ssh process per batch with no session pool, host registry or installer, and already landed; the finding records the owner to extend if a second facility later needs remote execution, which the plan already commits to deciding then.
findings.text: §3 adds an ambix remote extractor that duplicates the ssh worker, process executor and msgpack array format already owned by codex's remote layer; the plan names the owner and states the reason (importing codex would make its graph, LLM and tool-installation dependencies a dependency of every ambix read) and defers a shared remote core to a later plan.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each new mechanism (deck converter, tokamap exporter, EDDB extractor, EQDB reader) is one entry point hiding substantial parsing, transport or collapse behaviour, not a spread of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 re-implements codex's remote-execution core rather than extending it; the plan names the owner, so the finding records it rather than blocks on it.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — with all four figures at 0, every section that adds surface accounts for it in its own text (§2 "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §3 "retires nothing, because ambix has no remote reader today" and "adds no `ambix data` command"; §4 "retires nothing inside ambix, because ambix has no deck reader today" and the probe-angle key retires the machine branch; §7 "retires nothing, because no equilibrium-database reader exists").
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searched and cites a mechanism per subsystem, but its §4 claim to retire the one `machine == "mast"` branch misses a second MAST-only probe-angle source and a hard-coded MAST catalogue on the §7 route.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one wrapper-shaped addition, §3's extractor over remote execution, states in its own text why codex's layer cannot be imported (`imas-codex`'s graph/LLM/tool-installation dependencies would become a dependency of every ambix read) and defers a shared core to its own plan.
